brief: We pick groceries and recipes for you based on a quiz, weekly box, around $90 a week. Targeting busy people who want to eat healthier without planning.

profile.business_summary: A weekly grocery and recipe subscription box curated via a quiz, priced at approximately $90 per week, targeting busy individuals seeking healthier eating options without the hassle of meal planning.

stated_claims: We pick groceries and recipes for you based on a quiz

relevant_tags.why: The core product is a weekly box containing recipes and curated groceries.
Operates as a recurring weekly box model.

Targets consumers looking to eat healthier through a DTC model.

note_signals.why: Pantrygood's audience values wellness and clean ingredients, aligning well with a healthy grocery service.

profile.gate_reason: The product, pricing, subscription model, and target audience are clearly defined, allowing for immediate campaign planning.

config.advertiser_summary: A weekly grocery and recipe subscription box curated via a quiz, priced at approximately $90 per week, targeting busy individuals seeking healthier eating options without the hassle of meal planning.

assumptions: subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
Margin not given; assumed 35% (typical for meal_kits) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $90 x 35% x 4.0 orders = $126.00.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $2.00 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.42, relative fit x1.40; 0.0280 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.40 (cap $2.00)
score 0.38, relative fit x1.32; 0.0280 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.32 (cap $1.89)
score 0.27, relative fit x1.11; 0.0280 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.11 (cap $1.59)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $2.00 cap (category default).
